prompt:
Repair this production reference sheet while keeping the established character designs, yellow tablet, gray laptop, identical red paper boat picture, routers and server. In the bottom network-route strip REMOVE the cables between tablet and its home router and between the other home router and laptop. Instead show short curved Wi-Fi wave arcs at ONLY those two local wireless links. Keep physical blue cables joining the intervening network routers and service server. Tablets and laptops have no Ethernet cable plugged in. All other devices and identities unchanged. Clean flat vector-like fills without grain, no letters or numbers.

Authoritative specification:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: A Message Crosses the Internet; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: An illustrative messaging-app route from Zoe’s tablet at home to Kit’s laptop in a different home, through a service server. Same picture of one red paper boat throughout. Actual data are coded signals, not tiny pictures, envelopes or beads inside wires. Schematic packet tiles are explicitly a model.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Zoe’s plain yellow-cased tablet; Kit’s plain gray laptop; Red paper boat picture; Two home routers, network routers, cable links and a service server
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: One picture ready to send, no private messages or names shown; ordinary home setting.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Zoe selects one red paper boat picture on her tablet. One picture ready to send, no private messages or names shown; ordinary home setting.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions. Reference-sheet override: any lettering requested by the opening page brief belongs only in that finished page. Keep this production reference board entirely unlabelled; no letters, numbers or pseudo-writing. Draw all surfaces with perfectly smooth solid vector-like color fills. No speckle, grain, watercolor, paper texture or 3D shading. Show ONLY this book’s explicitly named subjects and props, with anatomically correct shapes and physically connected parts. No extra animals, humans or decorative objects. Each diagram must reflect actual mechanisms; avoid fantasy decorative arrows.

visualReview.note: Inspected installed WebP: locked Kit/Zoe, yellow tablet/gray laptop, red paper boat picture, Wi-Fi-only device-to-home-router links and wired provider/server links. Clean unlettered reference.
